title: Async queue backpressure surge and hybrid batch degradation — incident follow-up
creator: Leah Patel
description: Summary: During a customer load spike on 2026-02-17 we observed repeated short-duration tail-latency spikes (95/99p) and a class of degraded throughput on the continuous batching path. This ticket captures the post-incident follow-ups: root-cause analysis, mitigation roadmap, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence and improve debugging signal. The incident produced intermittent customer-facing increased latencies for batched text-generation routes; overall error rates were unchanged but p95/p99 token latencies increased ~2-4x for 8 minutes in the critical region.
incident_summary: 2026-02-17 15:12 UTC — sudden rise in batch_wait_time and bursty backpressure on allocator. The async queue prioritized small, high-priority requests and caused repeated micro-starvation of standard slots. KV-cache warm-up + transient kernel handoff amplified stalls. Result: multiple small batches queued repeatedly and long-tail latency spikes for medium-sized requests.
timeline: 2026-02-17T15:12Z — Alert: p99 token latency > 2x baseline for /v1/generate on cluster us-west-2
2026-02-17T15:14Z — Oncall (Omar) paged; initial mitigation: increase coalescer timeout from 8ms -> 16ms (temporary).
2026-02-17T15:20Z — Observed partial improvement; however p95 remained elevated. Noted repeated small-batch churn on coalescer and that batch allocator logs show high preemption of medium slots.
2026-02-17T15:35Z — Reverted experimental priority lane config that had been rolled 24h prior (flag: batcher.priority_hybrid=true).
2026-02-17T15:47Z — Final mitigation: disabled priority preemption and restored deterministic slot allocation; metrics returned to baseline by 15:55Z.
2026-02-17T16:10Z — Incident declared resolved; post-incident analysis begun.
2026-02-18T10:00Z — Deep dive started with runtime/core & scheduler owners (Aisha, Marco, Omar).
root_cause: Combination of a recently-introduced hybrid priority allocator (rolled to reduce head-of-line latency for tiny requests) and async queue backpressure interactions. Under bursty load the allocator frequently preempted medium slots to service high-priority tiny requests; preemption triggered rapid KV-cache context switches and kernel selection churn which prolonged batch formation windows and amplified tail latency. Lack of per-slot wait-time telemetry and insufficient canary coverage for mixed-size traffic allowed the regression to reach production.
mitigations: Short-term: revert priority_preemption flag (done during incident).
Short-term: increased coalescer timeout to reduce oscillation; reverted after stability verified (temporary).
Medium-term: add per-slot wait_time_percentiles and preemption_count metrics to the batch coordinator and surface in Console route dashboards.
Medium-term: implement a 'grace period' on preemption so a slot only gets preempted if it has been idle < X ms (configurable), avoiding thrashing under bursty mixes.

Long-term: redesign hybrid allocator to account for cumulative slot cost (KV-warmup penalty + kernel-switch overhead) when deciding preemption; prefer batching that reduces total cost rather than individual request latency.
Operational: create a canary scenario for mixed traffic sizes (tiny + medium) in perf lab and run nightly regression tests.
Observability: add Alert rule: sustained batch_wait_time_p95 > 1.5x baseline for 3m AND preemption_count_rate > threshold.
action_items: (Omar) Instrumentation: add metrics batch_slot_wait_p50/p95/p99 and batch_preemption_count to coordinator — estimate 3 points — due 2026-03-05 — PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/2345

(Aisha Chen) Scheduling logic: add configurable preemption_grace_ms and unit tests for no-thrash scenarios — estimate 5 points — due 2026-03-12 — Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/display/BATCH/Hybrid+Allocator+Redesign

(Marco Ruiz) Perf lab: create mixed-traffic canary (tiny/medium/high-concurrency) and nightly job to run baseline comparisons — estimate 3 points — due 2026-03-15 — Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/display/BATCH/Canary+Traffic

(Leah Patel) Console: add batch_wait_time_p95 panel to /runtime/latency route dashboard and a composite alert — estimate 2 points — due 2026-03-08 — Dashboard URL: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rt-batches
(SRE) Ops runbook update: include preemption rollback steps and playbook for extended RK (release keep) — estimate 1 point — due 2026-03-07
tests_planned: Unit tests for preemption_grace behavior across slot sizes.
Load test: mixed-size workload (60% tiny, 30% medium, 10% large) with concurrency ramp to surface thrashing.
Chaos test: intermittent kernel-selection delay injected to emulate KV-cache warmup penalty and observe batching resilience.
review_feedback: PM (Rina Kapoor): prefer a low-risk rollout (canary -> gradual ramp) and tie QoS metrics to rollout gates.
Design (Priyanka Rao): ensure allocator honors per-tenant isolation — preemption should be tenant-aware to avoid cross-tenant starvation.
Security (Hiro Tanaka): no direct secrets impact; flagged to include KMS path in runbook where we record audit links for canary jobs.
notes: Decision log: revert-first approach for unknown allocator regressions proved correct; we need safer rollout gates for scheduler flags.
Trade-offs discussed: increasing coalescer timeout reduces qps for tiny requests but stabilizes medium p95; decided to prefer stability while redesigning allocator.
Follow-up sync scheduled: 2026-03-02 16:00 UTC with runtime, platform, and SRE to agree on rollout plan for allocator changes.
